bug_semantics: A remote unauthenticated client can repeatedly submit candidate administrator passwords to either the Administration Console's /j_security_check flow or the Management REST /management/domain flow. Each request independently reaches credential verification, and a bad credential only produces the normal login failure/HTTP 401 response: the vulnerable implementation keeps no failure count across requests and applies no delay, throttle, concurrent-attempt cap, or account/host lockout. Consequently an attacker can make an unbounded series of guesses and a later correct password is still accepted.
flaw_origin: The smallest reconstructed code-origin commit is javaee/glassfish commit 0fee8143d3ad099bb7b4583785693957c838523a: it created RestAdapter.java as the remotely exposed, security-wrapped REST management adapter, called authenticate for every request, and returned an immediate 401 on failure without retaining or consulting any failed-attempt state. The later c1f1b2942b2a657eb61e707069dd4ea9d3e3a730 added AdminConsoleAuthModule.java and extended the same unrestricted behavior to the console login route. Eclipse commit 571714739b23e16c4c90d5229b806433920b3bcb is only the 2018 aggregate import of that already-vulnerable predecessor history, not the real BIC.
ai_marker: absent: the raw BIC commit object identifies both author and committer as Rajeshwar Patil <rajeshwar@java.net>; its message has only the human-written description, svn path/revision metadata, and Former-commit-id metadata, with no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI-tool trailer, or bot identity.
evidence: First-party disclosure: https://gitlab.eclipse.org/security/vulnerability-reports/-/issues/231 identifies unauthenticated brute-force access through /j_security_check (j_password) and /management/domain (Authorization) and demonstrates 50 failures followed by a successful 51st login; https://gitlab.eclipse.org/security/cve-assignment/-/issues/33 states that GlassFish 7.0.16 or earlier has no failed-login limit, while the assigned GHSA bundle records the subsequently widened Maven range <=7.0.25. BIC reconstruction: `git show 0fee8143d3ad099bb7b4583785693957c838523a -- v3/admin/rest/src/main/java/org/glassfish/admin/rest/RestAdapter.java` in the archived public javaee/glassfish history shows a new 302-line adapter; service() calls authenticate before dispatch (original lines 113-148), authenticate(Request, ServerEnvironmentImpl) delegates each request to AdminAuthenticator (174-184), and a false result is immediately returned as HTTP 401 with WWW-Authenticate BASIC (212-230), with no attempt counter or backoff. `git cat-file -p 0fee8143d3ad099bb7b4583785693957c838523a` gives the sole parent 7975999a9bce3825ec4b162a92c1c51f00b0f4f1 and the stated human author/committer; `git ls-tree -r --name-only 7975999a9bce3825ec4b162a92c1c51f00b0f4f1 -- v3/admin/rest/src/main/java/org/glassfish/admin/rest/RestAdapter.java` returns no entry, directly proving parent-tree absence. `git show --stat c1f1b2942b2a657eb61e707069dd4ea9d3e3a730` shows the later one-file, 245-line addition of AdminConsoleAuthModule.java, and its parent 2dc31199f4f4963ed93fef32681248aa7c697901 likewise has no such path. `git tag --contains 0fee8143d3ad099bb7b4583785693957c838523a` includes 3.0.1, 3.1.2, 4.1.x, and 5.0.x; the vulnerable implementation was then imported into the Eclipse repository by root aggregate 571714739b23e16c4c90d5229b806433920b3bcb, well before affected 7.0.x. Immediately before the fix, `git blame -L 230,268 0a99606e18291a106b680b671cdfb97b2abab7be -- nucleus/admin/util/src/main/java/com/sun/enterprise/admin/util/GenericAdminAuthenticator.java` shows authService.login followed by success return or rethrow of LoginException, still without cross-request tracking. Fix lifecycle: direct commit https://github.com/eclipse-ee4j/glassfish/commit/8577a9d602ad76354c3625673979038848aa3142 creates AuthenticationAttemptTracker.java and wires GenericAdminAuthenticator to check before authentication, reset on success, and record/delay on failure; RestAdapter maps saturation to HTTP 429 and AdminConsoleAuthModule forwards the client host. Merge commit https://github.com/eclipse-ee4j/glassfish/commit/6cab4ce3aad9bc65b52bc761a4aa88634a2bd0aa lands the completed fix series as PR https://github.com/eclipse-ee4j/glassfish/pull/26026, whose first-party description explicitly covers both the console and REST API. Tag checks resolve 7.0.25 to commit 17c9f164606e47efbc58907a97ad351a7f54089e and 8.0.2 to 5225f2e584d7eff969cd39ca26aa67e5dd828736; `git merge-base --is-ancestor 6cab4ce...` fails for both, and the 7.0.25 tree has no AuthenticationAttemptTracker.java. The same ancestry check succeeds for 8.0.3 commit 00c8ff1c98b5a1fabfc4c8e922d9bd7398908c77, establishing 8.0.3 as a released fixed boundary while the advisory's 7.x line remains unpatched through 7.0.25.
reasoning: The disclosure describes one omission shared by two remotely reachable administrator-authentication paths: failures are stateless and unlimited. History of the current Eclipse file alone misleadingly assigns most vulnerable lines to the parentless 2018 Initial Contribution. Decomposing that aggregate against the public predecessor history identifies 0fee8143d3ad099bb7b4583785693957c838523a as the smallest active commit that first made the management REST surface authenticate remote requests without any failure limiter; its immediate parent lacks the entire adapter, so the relevant behavior is absent rather than merely moved or reformatted. The console-specific module was added later by c1f1b2942b2a657eb61e707069dd4ea9d3e3a730, which expands the attack surface but cannot displace the earlier REST BIC. Subsequent authenticator rewrites and the Eclipse migration preserved the omission, so they are refactors/imports rather than introducers. The fix first adds exactly the missing stateful invariant: track failures by user/remote host, exponentially delay repeated failures, cap concurrent delayed requests with 429, and clear state after success. It is absent from the last vulnerable 7.x tag and 8.0.2 and present in 8.0.3, satisfying the version boundary. Finally, the AI decision uses only the raw 2009 BIC commit object: it has human author/committer identities and no AI marker or AI/bot trailer. Therefore the causal BIC is proven and the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
